evidence.description: DateFormatter is instantiated inside a computed property, which is expensive and inefficient for repeated access.

candidates.explanation: The DateFormatter is created every time the 'localizedMonthAndYear' property is accessed. DateFormatter is an expensive object to initialize and should ideally be reused or stored as a static constant.
candidates.title: Inefficient Object Creation

evidence.description: DateFormatter is instantiated inside a method that may be called frequently.

candidates.explanation: Like the previous finding, the DateFormatter in 'fetchAndUpdate' is instantiated on every call. Since the format and time zone are static, this should be optimized for performance.
candidates.title: Inefficient Object Creation

evidence.description: The response from the URLSession is decoded using JSONSerialization first, then the data is converted back to Data to be decoded by JSONDecoder.

candidates.explanation: The code performs unnecessary conversions by using JSONSerialization to get a dictionary, then converting that dictionary back into Data (JSONSerialization.data(withJSONObject:)) just to use JSONDecoder. This is inefficient and can lead to data loss or overhead.
candidates.title: Redundant Data Conversion

evidence.description: The actor uses a singleton pattern with a public static shared property.
The initializer is internal, which is standard for singletons, but the actor itself is public.

candidates.explanation: While common, using a singleton pattern with a Swift Actor can sometimes lead to architectural issues regarding state management and testing, as it provides a global shared state.
candidates.title: Singleton Pattern with Actor
